facts.text: An approximately 150 μm FeCoNiCrAl bond coat was deposited on Inconel 718 using the low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 process with propylene fuel.
The selected deposition condition used the medium air/fuel-pressure setting, a 63 mm 3L4 nozzle, and a 2.75 mm powder injector.
The Inconel 718 substrate was preheated to 155 °C during spraying.
The coated specimens were isothermally oxidized in air at 1000, 1100, and 1150 °C for up to 50 h.
After oxidation, specimens were air-cooled for approximately 5 min and repeatedly weighed to determine mass gain.
The low coating porosity restricted oxygen ingress and internal oxidation.
Outward diffusion and oxidation of Al produced a protective, predominantly Al2O3 thermally grown oxide layer.
Sluggish elemental diffusion in the HEA limited oxide transport and substantial chromia or spinel mixed-oxide formation.
The selected medium-pressure condition increased deposition efficiency relative to the low- and high-pressure HVAF-i7 settings.
Deposition efficiency was 79% at medium pressure, compared with 73% at low pressure and 53% at high pressure.
The selected medium-pressure condition reduced coating porosity relative to the low- and high-pressure settings.
Porosity was 0.2% at medium pressure, compared with 0.8% at low pressure and 1.8% at high pressure.
